titleEn: Getting a big head start on holiday shopping can benefit retailers and consumers alike
titleZh: 提前开始节日购物，如何让商家与消费者同时获益
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Amazon, Costco, Target, Walmart and other retailers begin their holiday sales as early as October.
paragraphs.zh: 亚马逊、好市多、塔吉特、沃尔玛和其他零售商最早从10月开始开始假日促销。

paragraphs.en: But there’s no need to rush to buy wool scarves, fuzzy throw blankets and the other holiday gifts on your list the second you spot some tinsel while shopping.
paragraphs.zh: 但是，没有必要急于购买羊毛围巾，模糊扔毯子和其他节日礼物清单上的第二个你看到一些金属丝，而购物。

paragraphs.en: As a finance professor who studies how people and companies make financial decisions, I can explain why the holiday shopping season starts so early: It can help retailers attract more customers while allowing cash-strapped shoppers to stretch purchases out across multiple paychecks. And, for people with deeper pockets, buying gifts early can help them avoid the stress that goes with last-minute shopping.
paragraphs.zh: 作为一名研究个人和公司如何做出财务决策的金融学教授，我可以解释为什么假日购物季会这么早开始：它可以帮助零售商吸引更多的顾客，同时让手头拮据的购物者可以在多个薪水支票上延长购买时间。而且，对于财力雄厚的人来说，提前购买礼物可以帮助他们避免最后一刻购物带来的压力。

paragraphs.en: Why retailers get such an early start
paragraphs.zh: 为什么零售商这么早就开始

paragraphs.en: Estimates for spending on holiday gifts, decor and the like between late 2026 and January 2027 range from about US$1 trillion to $1.7 trillion in the U.S.
paragraphs.zh: 据估计，2026年底至2027年1月期间，美国在节日礼物、装饰等方面的支出约为1万亿至1.7万亿美元。

paragraphs.en: Some 29% of Americans plan to shell out their share of those large sums in early to mid-December this holiday season, while 17% will shop on Black Friday, the day after Thanksgiving, according to the Bank of America Holiday Spending survey.
paragraphs.zh: 美国银行假日消费调查显示，约29%的美国人计划在12月初至12月中旬的假期中支付大笔款项，17%的人将在感恩节后的黑色星期五购物。

paragraphs.en: But many people like to shop for holiday gifts early – meaning before Halloween. Some do this out of necessity: They can’t afford to buy all the gifts they want to give unless they spread the cost over multiple paychecks.
paragraphs.zh: 但很多人喜欢早早地--也就是在万圣节之前--去买节日礼物。有些人是出于必要才这么做的：他们买不起所有想送的礼物，除非他们把这些费用分摊到多份薪水上。

paragraphs.en: For others, it’s more of a preference. In a 2025 survey, about 54% of early shoppers said they want to manage their budgets gradually. In addition, 41% said they buy gifts early to avoid the stress associated with last-minute shopping.
paragraphs.zh: 对其他人来说，这更像是一种偏好。在2025年的一项调查中，约54%的提前购物者表示，他们希望逐步管理自己的预算。此外，41%的人表示，他们提前购买礼物是为了避免最后一刻购物带来的压力。

paragraphs.en: Retailers are adjusting by getting an early start on holiday sales and promoting seasonal items. By offering customers deals months before gift-giving commences, they can encourage even more people to join the early birds.
paragraphs.zh: 零售商们正在通过提前开始假日销售和促销季节性商品来进行调整。通过在送礼开始前几个月向顾客提供优惠，他们可以鼓励更多的人加入早起的人。

paragraphs.en: And by launching promotions in October, they might secure sales that otherwise would go to their competitors later in the season.
paragraphs.zh: 通过在10月推出促销活动，他们可能会确保销售，否则将在本赛季晚些时候去他们的竞争对手。

paragraphs.en: A longer selling season offers other advantages to retailers. It may ease pressure on their supply chain and logistics, since they can receive seasonal orders over three months instead of one or two. This minimizes shipping difficulties and lowers warehouse overhead costs.
paragraphs.zh: 较长的销售季节为零售商提供了其他优势。这可能会减轻他们的供应链和物流压力，因为他们可以在三个月内而不是一两个月内收到季节性订单。这可以最大限度地减少运输困难，降低仓库管理费用。

paragraphs.en: Building more time into the calendar to move seasonal inventory gives retailers more opportunities to sell those items. However, an earlier shopping season does not necessarily increase consumer spending overall. Some purchases may simply shift from December to October.
paragraphs.zh: 在日历中留出更多时间来转移季节性库存，使零售商有更多机会销售这些商品。然而，购物季节提前并不一定会增加消费者的整体支出。一些购买可能只是从12月转移到10月。

paragraphs.en: Beware of some early-shopping pitfalls
paragraphs.zh: 小心一些早期购物的陷阱

paragraphs.en: To make sure that buying gifts long before the holidays occur is a wise move, early shoppers should read vendors’ fine print and research their return policies.
paragraphs.zh: 为了确保在节日到来之前购买礼物是明智之举，早期购物者应该阅读供应商的细则并研究他们的退货政策。

paragraphs.en: Many big retailers are making their return policies more restrictive by shortening the length of time you can return purchases and adding return/restocking fees.
paragraphs.zh: 许多大型零售商通过缩短退货时间和增加退货/补货费用，使他们的退货政策更加严格。

paragraphs.en: In some cases, the deadline you face for returning an item could fall before the holidays. For example, Best Buy’s extended policy takes effect in 2026 only for purchases made on or after Oct. 30. Target similarly restricts its holiday-season returns window to items bought on or after Nov. 1.
paragraphs.zh: 在某些情况下，您面临的退货截止日期可能会在假期之前。例如，百思买的延长政策将于2026年生效，仅适用于10月30日或之后购买的商品。Target也将其假日退货窗口限制为11月30日或之后购买的商品。1.

paragraphs.en: Amazon extended its holiday return policy in 2026. If you buy an item from Nov. 1 to Dec. 31, it can be returned until Jan. 31, 2027, except for Apple products, which can be returned until Jan. 15. Anyone who bought gifts beforehand will likely be subject to a standard 30-day return policy, which will expire long before Christmas.
paragraphs.zh: 亚马逊在2026年延长了其假日退货政策。如果你在11月1日至12月31日期间购买商品，它可以在2027年1月31日之前退货，但苹果产品除外，它可以在1月15日之前退货。任何提前购买礼物的人都可能会受到标准的30天退货政策的约束，该政策将在圣诞节前很久到期。

paragraphs.en: When buying early makes financial sense
paragraphs.zh: 当早期购买具有财务意义时

paragraphs.en: Shopping early is smart when the costs of waiting could outweigh the potential benefits of spending your money earlier than otherwise necessary.
paragraphs.zh: 当等待的成本可能超过提前花钱的潜在好处时，提前购物是明智的。

paragraphs.en: For example, if a popular wool scarf that was priced at $100 in October is out of stock on Amazon by November, the supply is gone, but demand remains high. If you want to buy it for your mom and ensure it arrives in time, you may need to get it from other retailers. Maybe you can find the scarf on a website but is selling for $150. If time has run out, you might have to pay, say, $30 more for expedited shipping, bringing the total to $180. Clearly, you would have been better off buying it early on at a lower price.
paragraphs.zh: 例如，如果一条10月份售价100美元的流行羊毛围巾在11月份在亚马逊上脱销，那么供应就没有了，但需求仍然很高。如果你想为你的妈妈买它并确保它及时到达，你可能需要从其他零售商那里购买。也许你可以在网站上找到这条围巾，但售价为150美元。如果时间已经用完，你可能不得不付钱，比如说，加快运输要多花30美元，使总额达到180美元。显然，你最好早点以较低的价格购买。

paragraphs.en: But that doesn’t mean you necessarily need to rush to buy a gift weeks or months ahead of when you’ll be placing it under a tree. First make sure that the price is in line with your expectations and what you’re willing to shell out.
paragraphs.zh: 但这并不意味着你一定要提前几周或几个月买一件礼物，首先要确保价格符合你的期望和你愿意付出的代价。

paragraphs.en: And you should do some comparison shopping to make sure other retailers aren’t charging less for the same or similar items.
paragraphs.zh: 你应该做一些比较购物，以确保其他零售商没有收取更少的相同或类似的项目。

paragraphs.en: Remember, waiting to do your holiday shopping until the last minute can lead to unnecessary costs, like rush shipping fees. The key is to have a budget, recognize when the price is right, and know when to stop shopping.
paragraphs.zh: 记住，等到最后一分钟才去购物会导致不必要的费用，比如匆忙的运费。关键是要有预算，知道什么时候价格合适，什么时候停止购物。
